data.summary: 1 Insight(s) from <ins_1>: 1 mandatory, 0 unusable. 2 recent Crumb(s), 3 proposal(s), 3 open question(s).

insights.title: One engine, one transaction, one close
insights.excerpt: Every bdc invocation opens one short-lived engine and closes it before it returns. Reads state the freshness of anything cached, and a handoff never refreshes.

open_questions.question: 5 Crumb(s) are waiting on review
open_questions.detail: run `bdc crumb list --state candidate`, then `bdc crumb review <id>... --state accepted|rejected --rationale ...`

open_questions.question: promoting to docs:docs/policy/ledger.md needs a human decision
open_questions.detail: a human grants it with `bdc authority <pp_2> --level default|mandatory --rationale ...`

open_questions.question: I concluded (0.80): Every bdc invocation opens one short-lived engine, performs one bounded transaction, and closes it. Reads state the freshness of anything cached. Right, partly right, or wrong?
open_questions.detail: answer it with `bdc ask answer <ask_4> --choice ...`, or decline it with `bdc ask skip <ask_4>`

recent_crumbs.excerpt: A cached tracker label was mistaken for live state, so every read states its freshness.
The engine holds an exclusive directory lock for the life of a command.
